decks.name: LeetCode #130 - Surrounded Regions
decks.description: Capture all regions surrounded by X by flipping O to X, except regions connected to board borders

cards.question: Surrounded Regions: Given an m x n matrix board containing 'X' and 'O', capture all regions that are 4-directionally surrounded by 'X'. A region is captured by flipping all 'O's into 'X's in that surrounded region. Note that regions on the border cannot be captured because they are not surrounded.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Mark border-connected O's, then flip remaining O's to X's. Key insight: O's connected to borders cannot be captured. First, run DFS from all border O's, temporarily marking them as T. DFS explores all connected O's recursively in four directions. After marking all unsurrounded O's as T, scan entire board: flip remaining O's to X's (these are surrounded), flip T's back to O's (these are unsurrounded). This approach avoids checking if each O is surrounded by examining connectivity from borders. Time O(m*n) visiting each cell once. Space O(m*n) for recursion stack in worst case.

solutions.timeDescription: We visit each cell at most twice: once during DFS marking phase from borders, and once during final conversion phase. DFS from borders visits only border-connected cells
solutions.spaceDescription: Recursion stack can go up to m*n depth in worst case when entire board is O's connected in a line from border
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given board [['X','X','X','X'],['X','O','O','X'],['X','X','O','X'],['X','O','X','X']]: Start DFS from borders. Border O at (3,1): mark as T, explore connected cells, mark (2,2) as T. No other border O's. Scan board: (1,1) is O (not T), flip to X. (1,2) is O (not T), flip to X. (2,2) is T, restore to O. (3,1) is T, restore to O. Result: [['X','X','X','X'],['X','X','X','X'],['X','X','O','X'],['X','O','X','X']]. Interior O's at (1,1) and (1,2) were surrounded and captured.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS to mark border-connected O's, then flip remaining O's to X's. Initialize queue with all border cells. Process queue: for each cell, if it's O, mark as T and add all four neighbors to queue. This explores all border-connected O's level by level. After BFS completes, scan board: flip remaining O's to X's (surrounded), flip T's to O's (unsurrounded). BFS avoids deep recursion by using queue for iterative exploration. Each cell added to queue at most once. Time O(m*n) visiting each cell once. Space O(m*n) for queue in worst case.

solutions.timeDescription: Initial scan to find border cells takes O(m*n). BFS visits each cell at most once. Final conversion scan takes O(m*n). Total is linear in board size
solutions.spaceDescription: Queue can hold up to m*n cells in worst case when entire board consists of O's connected to borders
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given board [['X','X','X','X'],['X','O','O','X'],['X','X','O','X'],['X','O','X','X']]: Initialize queue with border cells. Border O at (3,1): enqueue. BFS: dequeue (3,1), mark as T, enqueue neighbors. Process (2,1), it's X, skip. Process (3,0), it's X, skip. Process (3,2), it's X, skip. Process (2,2), mark as T, enqueue neighbors. Process all neighbors of (2,2). BFS completes. Scan board: (1,1) and (1,2) are O (not marked as T), flip to X. (2,2) and (3,1) are T, restore to O. Same result as DFS.

solutions.name: Disjoint Set Union
solutions.explanation: Use Union-Find to group border-connected O's, then flip non-connected O's. Create DSU with extra dummy node representing borders. Iterate through board: for border O's, union with dummy node. For interior O's, union with adjacent O's. After building connected components, scan board: cells not connected to dummy node are surrounded, flip to X. DSU with path compression and union by size ensures efficient operations. This approach groups cells by connectivity. Time O(m*n) with amortized O(α(m*n)) per operation. Space O(m*n) for parent and size arrays.

solutions.timeDescription: We iterate through all cells twice: once to build unions and once to check connectivity. Each union and find operation is nearly O(1) amortized due to path compression and union by size
solutions.spaceDescription: DSU parent and size arrays store m*n+1 entries to represent all cells plus the dummy border node
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given board [['X','X','X','X'],['X','O','O','X'],['X','X','O','X'],['X','O','X','X']]: DSU with dummy node at index ROWS*COLS=16. Border O at (3,1): union(16, 13). Interior O at (1,1): check neighbors, (1,2) is O, union(5, 6). Interior O at (1,2): check neighbors, (1,1) already in same set, (2,2) is O, union(6, 10). Interior O at (2,2): neighbors processed, union(10, 13) connects to border. Final check: (1,1) and (1,2) not connected to node 16, flip to X. (2,2) and (3,1) connected to node 16, keep as O. Result captures surrounded regions.
